why: Y has no 30-day retention for raw notes (R7). Its spec says "Nothing is hard-deleted after commit" and stores `notes_text` on meetings indefinitely. X builds a nightly cron that "delete[s] `notes` past `delete_after`", keeps quotes, and tests it at day 23 and day 31.

Y's input limit breaks the stated note sizes (R2). "notes up to 50,000 characters" is roughly 8–9K words, so the 15,000-word Zoom transcripts would be rejected. X allows up to 30,000 words and does the math: "15,000 words is about 20–27K tokens… no chunking."

X fits a non-technical PM who needs a URL on a budget (R12, R13). It uses one Cloudflare project with auto-deploy, a click-by-click setup guide, and a costed budget ("~$10–20") with a "$15" Anthropic spend cap. Y is "host-agnostic. Any Node 20+ host plus managed Postgres", needs Docker locally, and never addresses cost or who deploys it.

X handles dates and owners more carefully (R4, R5, R6). It uses IST everywhere, adds an "Owner not in quote" check, and never gives vague phrases a date. Its eval has explicit launch bars: "0 items with a *confident* owner that is wrong", "≥ 95%" found. Y uses the browser time zone for overdue, and its duplicate detection only compares items "in the same meeting", which misses R16's cross-meeting case.

Y wins on code-level executability: full TDD code for every task. But X is also highly executable. Its phases are gated ("stop, wait for OK"), each has a named test command, and paid eval runs need approval. X's weaknesses, heavy v1 scope (locks, take-over, stats) against a 2-week target and no mention of Hinglish, don't outweigh Y's missed requirements.
